Hi team 1

Attached are two quick sketches (spreadsheet) 1 I'm summarizing the key lines here so it's easy to review in-line: 

Scenario A (Low license / higher unit):
- Term license (12mo) per cluster: $35k/mo per cluster
- Support: Standard (email + slack, 9x5) included; Enterprise add-on $8k/mo for named CSE + 24x5 on-call
- Unit rate: $1,850 per 1M tokens (applies to all usage)
- Example @90M tokens: token cost = $166,500/mo + license $35k = $201,500/mo (plus support if selected)

Scenario B (Higher license / lower unit):
- Term license (12mo) per cluster: $110k/mo per cluster
- Support: Enterprise included (named CSE + 24x5)
- Unit rate: $900 per 1M tokens
- Example @90M tokens: token cost = $81,000/mo + license $110k = $191,000/mo (lower total at higher volume)

Notes / tradeoffs:
- Scenario A benefits teams with unpredictable/low volumes because of lower fixed commitment.
- Scenario B is better for predictable, higher-volume deployments where procurement prefers fixed operational cost and bundled support.
- Onboarding/setup: one-time $25k for VPC onboarding, SOC2 evidence transfer, and basic performance tuning (can be amortized).

I can drop these numbers into a simple slide and include side-by-side totals at 25M / 90M / 220M tokens if that would be helpful for procurement.

Ben
